summary: B is preferable because its out-of-scope retry change is narrower and its retry test verifies the multipart payload on every attempt. Both patches nevertheless violate the explicit requirement to route Upload through FilesService.Add.
reasons: Both add the required Upload signature, validate filename/content, use multipartbody.NewFile with field "file", and propagate its errors.
Both duplicate Add's option handling, Raw.Do call, response decoding, and missing-data error instead of delegating to Add, creating the maintenance divergence the contract explicitly forbids.

B limits generic retry changes to seekable readers; A eagerly buffers every otherwise-unrecognized io.Reader across the SDK, introducing potentially unbounded memory use and changed read/error timing.
B's Upload retry test parses the multipart form and verifies file content on both attempts. A's retry test only discards each body, so it would not catch an empty or corrupted replay.
risks_a: The RawClient change globally buffers arbitrary reader bodies whenever retries are not disabled, a substantial unrelated semantic and resource-usage change.
Upload bypasses Add despite the frozen contract.
The added RawClient machinery and documentation substantially expand scope beyond the requested convenience API.
risks_b: Upload also bypasses Add, duplicating lower-level behavior.
enableBodyReplay returns the same mutable seeker from GetBody rather than an independent body, which is less robust than standard GetBody semantics and changes caller-reader closing behavior.
The Upload tests omit the explicitly requested source-reader-error case and do not verify FilesOption forwarding.
